items.title: Systemic two-column TOC corruption -- most of OR.S02 through OR.S16 titles/parenting are wrong
items.summary: The printed Toronto Notes TOC for this chapter (raw OCR of pdf 1089) is a genuine two-column layout: left column runs Acronyms->Basic Anatomy Review->Fractures General Principles->Articular Cartilage->Orthopedic X-Ray Imaging->Orthopedic Emergencies->Shoulder->Humerus->Elbow->Radius and Ulna Shaft Fractures->Wrist->Hand->Spine->Pelvis->Hip; right column runs Femur->Knee->Patella->Tibia->Ankle->Foot->Pediatric Orthopedics->Bone Tumours->Common Medications->Landmark Orthopedic Trials->References. The automated toc_inventory.json extraction read both columns as a single interleaved stream, merging left-column row N with right-column row N into one garbled node title for most of the chapter (e.g. OR.S10 'Rotator Cuff Disease Ankle'), silently dropped entire right-column sections/children that had no same-row-index left-column partner to merge into (Fractures General Principles, Articular Cartilage, Orthopedic X-Ray Imaging, the Orthopedic Emergencies and Shoulder section headers themselves, Femur, most of Knee's 8 children, Tibial Shaft Fracture, Achilles tendon pathology, Plantar Fasciitis, Bunions -- 5 of these are also independently flagged UNRESOLVED in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json), and mis-parented three real Spine children (Fractures of the Spine, Cervical Spine, Thoracolumbar Spine) under the unrelated References section. Resolved via raw OCR of the TOC page plus ~25 spot-verification reads of body pages across the full pdf 1089-1141 range, cross-checked against the printed two-column structure and heading-adjacency at every point checked; no instance of my reconstructed left/right column ordering conflicted with body-page content. Full correction and per-unit citations are in study_units.json's methodology_note and each unit's structural_rationale.
items.recommended_action: Reviewer should spot-check a handful of the 75 reconstructed study units against the source PDF page images (not just raw OCR text, which was the only evidence used here) -- particularly the Femur/Knee/Foot units sourced entirely from synthetic UNCATALOGUED ids, since no toc_inventory.json node exists for them at all.
